Subject: Request: performance deep-dive + demo (load targets)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again — HyperCloud is excited to move from evaluation to a performance validation phase. We’d like a technical deep-dive/demo focused exclusively on performance: sustained token throughput and end-to-end latency under our workload. High-level asks: 
- Validate sustained token throughput around 20k–25k tokens/s for our common prompt mix (short answer + 2-step chains).
- Measure p99 and p95 latencies for sequences up to 8k tokens (we have streaming output in prod).
- Walk through autoscaling/fallback behavior under a burst scenario (20% traffic spike).

We’re targeting the week of July 24–28 for the run and would like a ~90-minute slot for the readout (run results + architecture review). Can you propose times and a short pre-run checklist? I attached our sample prompt set (hypercloud_sample_prompts.json).

Also looping Ben (PO) and our eng team for availability.

Thanks,
Anna Ruiz

Hi Anna — great to hear and thanks for the prompt set.

We can do a combined run + architecture review. Proposed approach: 
1) Pre-run checklist (30–60m remote): confirm tokenization, seq length distribution, and sample traffic profile.
2) Load run (3–4 hours): ramp + sustained window to hit 20k–25k tokens/s, with telemetry (CPU/GPU, kernel hotpaths, KV cache hit rates).
3) Readout (60–90m): p50/p95/p99, cost estimates, recommended runtime knobs (batching, quantization), and fallback plan.

Availability windows (PDT): July 25 — 08:00–12:00 or July 27 — 13:00–17:00. Which works for HyperCloud?

I’m attaching our runbook and a Mutual Action Plan template to speed sign-off. Also, Marcus will call out runtime config suggestions.

— Sofia

Quick technical notes before we lock a slot — tagging details so HyperCloud can validate test harness compatibility: 
- GPU pool: we’ll provision 4x A800s in a dedicated burst cluster for the run. Expect sustained kernel-level throughput for autoregressive models with 8-bit quantization.
- Batching profile: aim for dynamic batching with a 48ms latency cap to preserve p95 targets — we’ll measure effective batch sizes during ramp.
- KV caching: if your prompt mix reuses prefixes we expect a 10–15% token reduction; please flag heavy prefix reuse.
- Instrumentation: please enable streaming traces on your side (request IDs) so we can correlate p99 spikes.

Can HyperCloud provide two sample trace IDs and a peak RPS target (requests/sec) so we can translate to tokens/sec? If you cannot, we’ll plan a conservative RPS->token conversion (we’ll share the formula).

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — that all looks reasonable. Two clarifications from our side: 
- Peak RPS: we expect ~550 rps for the short-answer flow; average token length ~45 tokens per request, peak buckets up to 180 tokens. We’ll convert to tokens/sec (~24.75k tokens/s at peak).
- Prefix reuse: about 18% of requests reuse a 120-token system prompt.

Availability: July 27, prefer 14:00 PDT for the run + 90-minute readout right after (we can block 14:00–16:00). I’ll share two sample trace IDs and our internal harness (link) in a follow-up.

Also, we prefer if Redwood runs the ramp and keeps HyperCloud on observer-only console access; HyperCloud will provide a read-only test account.

— Anna
